linux_runtime_pr209_20261024.scope: Standalone development reconciliation against base478, incorporating linux-baseline and PR209 runtime features; updated2026-10-25. Manifest1-7 with local DIT7 and preserved Llama hi/lo sub-block attention. GGUF Q/K/Q8-head corrections, checked dense head dimensions, flash streams through8192, explicit paired probabilities and unsupported-window refusal. Includes synthetic --bench-kernel seek fix, compact5120 packing regression, and explicit experimental bfp16_hilo block input (9/4 bytes; native F32 output), independent host-pack tests and fail-closed incompatible-scope metadata. Not a sequential patch series or default promotion.

gemma4_bfp16_prefill_20261030.note: the dense block route's GEMMs on gemm_bfp16 (OPEN-PREFILL-BFP16 on the dense kind): manifest_version 4 (the bfp16_gemm pack op, row0 / n_total, and the bfp16 step format with n_pad; a bfp16 step reads exactly a bfp16_gemm weight, dense routes only), bfp16_gemm from a GGUF tensor's own blocks (embed_row) as well as q4nx q4_1 chunks, the activation packer and the c-tiled output read back as [N, T] or token rows, act * up encoded straight into the down projection's A operand (act_bfp16_a), and the prefill route chosen in the GGUF view too, where a GGUF-direct set carries its routes (fast = gemm_block, lean = the variant). bfp16.hpp is the granite branch's (openflowlm-next 07e635b) plus bfp16_c_offset. A diff over base plus the five earlier Gemma 4 patches

gemma4_prefill_pipeline_20261030.note: the dense layer-major prompt step-major (dense_layer_staged, on unless OFLM_OPEN_STAGE_MAJOR=0): qkv3 over every block with each block's attention host half under the next block's GEMM, the attention products over every (block, kv head), then o / up / gate / down over the blocks in pairs, one run outstanding and #1 twins of every x / y / attn_block global (pipeline()); each block's operations unchanged, so the same bits. The bfp16 route's GELU-tanh act in fp32 on AVX2 fused with act * up and the encode (gelu_bfp16_a, OFLM_OPEN_GELU32=0 keeps act_fp64). The A-operand encoders write in memory order and bfp16_encode_block takes its exponent maximum on the vector unit. attn_block's optional kernels_shl: qsplit's hi / lo scores as one product of 2 m rows (OFLM_OPEN_ATTN_SHL=0 off). The bfp16_gemm packer without per-block divisions, and a pack weight zeroes only the bytes no op writes (pools::unwritten). --prefill-mode accurate is lean. Without a bit changed, attention_prep takes rope angles once a position, up writes its own output pair (@up), gate encodes h straight into its down job's x and reuses up's x twin, qkv3 rows go straight into q / k / v (bfp16_rows_parts), and the stacked scores' softmax sums hi + lo as it reads them (softmax_chunk_sum); OFLM_OPEN_PIPE_LOG prints per-step host and wait times. A diff over base plus the six earlier Gemma 4 patches

gemma4_q40_gguf_20261030.note: std_perm_gguf's third chunk law: a 4608-B pool chunk (the Q4_0-native GGUF view, recipes/gemma4.py G4_Q40) holds the bf16 d plane and the codes, the cores taking m = -8 d (gemv_q4.h GEMV_Q4_0_NATIVE, gemm_q4_dequant.h GQD_Q4_0); only Q4_0 tensors pack into it, anything else is refused. gguf_pack_test checks it against the q4_1 law's d plane and codes, that law's m against -8 d, and that a Q4_1 tensor is refused. A diff over base plus the seven earlier Gemma 4 patches

gemma4_kvslice_20261030.note: per-core KV windows (OPEN-ATTN-KVSLICE) in this runtime: the manifest's kernel `kvslice` (2 or 4 rows an element, attnpos only, rb 1), attnpos tables over several window fills (each fill's length patched to the window padded to whole elements times its own words a row, its offset to its compiled in-row base plus the window's first row), and kvslice - 1 rows of KV slack. stream_patch.hpp's kvslice parts are phlegm's own header's (open_kernels/harness), without its rb_win, slot and attnposv additions. kvslice_patch_test checks Gemma 4's local (four fills, 1024-row window) and global (two fills) streams at positions 0..4095. Gemma 4's dx_local / dx kernels carry kvslice 4 (recipes/gemma4.py dx_attention); the test covers 2 and 4. A diff over base plus the eight earlier Gemma 4 patches
